note: Adapted from the English description of Hill 1925; Froggatt 1896 named the species from the alate, and Hill first described the soldier and supplemented the alate. The original's 'Queen' and 'King' sections are dewinged alates; the soldier head width is defective in the scanned text and is therefore not cited. Measurements in millimetres.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: the postmentum narrows markedly posteriorly, its narrowest part about one fifth of the head width; antennae 13—15-segmented, usually 13; mandibles short and stout, each with 3 short, broad, indistinct teeth; pronotum kidney-shaped, the width slightly more than twice the length; legs short and stout, the femora thickened and almost as wide as the tibiae. Alate: head and pronotum almost black, the posterior and lateral margins of the pronotum and the lower margin of the genae folded upwards.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head very dark brown, almost black; mesonotum and metanotum slightly paler; venter, labrum, palps and antennae brown (argus-brown); femora, tarsi and the last two sternites almost as dark as the mesonotum; anteclypeus transparent, ochraceous in the middle. Head finely shagreened, almost without setae except on the frons, broadly rounded posteriorly and laterally to the compound eyes; the middle of the frons slightly concave, with small grooves converging towards the centre. Compound eyes medium-sized (0.342 × 0.342) and protruding, the distance from their lower margin to the lower margin of the head about half a compound eye diameter; the lower margin of the genae folded upwards as at the pronotum. Ocelli small, broadly oval (length 0.114), close to but not touching the compound eyes. Postclypeus very short, paler than the vertex, without setae, the anterior margin slightly arcuate. Labrum short and very wide, about twice as long as wide, the anterior margin truncate, with very few setae. Antennae 15-segmented, length 1.70. Measurements (mm): total body length male 7.00; head length (to the tip of the labrum) 1.65—1.75; head length (to the frontoclypeal suture) 1.25; head width 1.45; pronotal length 0.85, width 1.42; hind tibia length 1.14.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head vinaceous rufous; mandibles black; anteclypeus transparent, ochraceous; labrum and antennae ochraceous; thorax, legs and abdomen buckthorn-brown. Sides of the head nearly parallel, bluntly rounded posteriorly, slightly narrowing forwards to the prominent anterolateral corners; frons sloping at 45° to the clypeus; clypeus and anteclypeus short, indistinct, the former with several moderately long and stout setae; apart from the labrum the head is almost hairless, the surface smooth and finely shagreened; labrum short and wide, with about 12 moderately long setae; postmentum narrowing markedly posteriorly, its narrowest part about one fifth of the head width; antennae 13—15-segmented, usually 13; mandibles short and stout, each with 3 short, broad, indistinct teeth. Pronotum slightly more than twice as wide as long, kidney-shaped. Legs short and stout, the femora thickened and almost as wide as the tibiae. Tergites and sternites with the same vestiture as the alate, the sternites with a few additional long red setae; cerci short and stout; styli moderately slender. Measurements (mm): total body length (value missing in the original); head length with mandibles 3.15—4.10; head length without mandibles 2.28—3.16; postmentum narrowest width 0.28; pronotal length 0.74—0.97, width 1.53—1.88; hind tibia length 1.25. Distribution: Frankston, Victoria (type locality), Melbourne, Belgrave, Beaconsfield; Dorrigo, Upper Lansdowne, New South Wales.
